statement: You are given an array nums of positive integers and an integer k.
A subarray is a non-empty run of adjacent elements. Return the length of the longest subarray whose elements add up to exactly k, or 0 if no subarray does.
Because every element is positive, extending a subarray always increases its sum, which is what lets a two-pointer window solve this in one pass.

examples.explanation: [3, 1, 1] at indices 2 to 4 adds up to 5. The other subarrays with sum 5, [2, 3] and [1, 4], are shorter.
The three 1s at indices 1 to 3 add up to 3. [1, 2] and [3] also sum to 3 but are shorter.
The whole array adds up to only 6, so no subarray reaches 10.
